Hi Alex —

Thanks again for the time last week. Per our MAP, we want to run the formal performance validation (baseline + production-like stress runs) ahead of your procurement sign-off. To keep the MAP and close timeline aligned, propose the following:

- Evaluation scope: latency (p50/p95/p99), throughput (tokens/sec & requests/sec), TTFT (time-to-first-token), and concurrency scaling to 64 live sessions.
- Test scenarios: short chat (avg 128 tokens), medium (512 tokens), long-seq (1,024 tokens).
- Baseline: cold start + 10m warmup; Stress: ramp to target concurrency over 20m, steady-state 60m, cooldown 10m.
- Suggested windows (low production impact): Nov 28 02:00-06:00 UTC or Nov 29 02:00-06:00 UTC. Please confirm which works and provide test account/service keys for a service account we can use from our load agents.

Deliverables from Redwood: updated MAP spreadsheet, runbook for the window, raw results CSV, and a short summary of any regressions + recommendations. We'll disable prefix caching for baseline runs to measure raw model latency, then enable cache for an additional pass.

Ask: can you also confirm any network egress policies that might block our load agents and whether a small IP allowlist is preferable?

Attachments: acme-map-v2.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

Thanks —
Rachel

Thanks Alex — and thanks Rachel for the MAP draft. A few operational details from our side so we can be ready by Nov 29:

- Redwood runbook (attached: redwood-load-runbook.md) will include agent IPs, SSH jumpbox instructions (if required), warmup sequences, and the exact ramp schedule. We will run three passes per scenario: baseline (no cache, no quant), cache-enabled, and quantized (if you approve).
- Target traffic profile:
  * Short chat: 400 rps sustained at 8k tokens/min aggregate
  * Medium: 200 rps sustained
  * Long: 50 rps (to exercise KV cache behavior)
  * Peak concurrency target: 64 concurrent sessions overall (distributed across models).
- Measurement: TTFT measured from request acceptance to first token for the first 20% of requests, then p50/p95/p99 across whole run; pod-level CPU/GPU utilization and GPU kernel times will be captured to help tune batch sizes.
- Stop criteria: if p95 latency > 2.5x expected or error rate > 1%, we'll abort and provide a post-mortem.

We'll also attach a small python script to replay deterministic prompts for reproducibility. Please confirm the allowlist CIDRs when you have them; otherwise we will use ephemeral agent pools from our us-west region and provide the ranges.

Attachments: redwood-load-runbook.md (text/markdown)

Subject: RE: MAP: Performance validation & load window coordination — Acme Corp (Results & next steps)

Alex / team —

We completed the scheduled runs last night (Nov 29 02:00-06:00 UTC). Quick highlights and next steps are below; full results attached.

Summary (aggregate across scenarios):
- Baseline (cache off): p50=78ms, p95=430ms, p99=920ms, TTFT median=110ms.
- Stress (ramp to 64 concurrency, cache on for second pass): sustained throughput 3.8k tokens/sec; request-level throughput 680 reqs/sec during steady-state.
- Observed tail increase under long-sequence scenario (1,024 tokens) — p95 rose to 1.2s during a short GPU GC spike on one pod.
- Error rate: 0.23% (transient 503s mostly tied to a single provisioning event).

Actionable recommendations:
1) For your SLAs, recommend we set an operational p95 target of 500ms for mixed workloads and enable the cache layer for production traffic; it drops token cost ~18% in our runs.
2) Apply a per-pod memory guard (we propose elevating eviction thresholds) to avoid the GC spike we saw under long sequences.
3) If you want to tighten latency, the quantized model reduced GPU utilization by ~22% at the cost of a small quality delta — recommend a short A/B on a subset of traffic post-rollout.

Attachments: load-results-20261129.csv (text/csv), acme-map-v2.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

Next steps:
- Redwood to provide a 30-minute readout for execs + SRE: propose Dec 1 15:00 UTC.
- Complete MAP finalization and send to procurement for signature by Dec 4.

Let me know if you want more granular per-pod traces; we can share sanitized kernel traces and Datadog links.

Thanks —
Rachel
